critical_code_review_comments: pin_auth.py refresh rotation correctly revokes old jti via upsert and mints a new pair with fresh jti — clean implementation.

Refresh endpoint correctly rejects revoked jti reuse with 401; logger warns about possible family compromise (good signal — consider implementing per-user family-revocation in a future hardening pass).
Logout endpoint is shape-uniform between valid/invalid/access-token inputs (always 200, just revoked:true/false) — correctly prevents oracle/info leak on token validity.
TTL index + unique jti index on revoked_tokens defined in _ensure_revoked_tokens_ttl(); scheduled as background task in init — guarantees auto-cleanup so denylist stays bounded.
JWT_SECRET_KEY is now 128-char hex in backend/.env, so token validity survives backend restarts (verified by file inspection; live restart was main-agent smoke-tested).
Verified routes/data_management.py uses {"_id": 0} projection on crm_configs.find(); printer_v2.py uses {"_id": 0} on customers.find_one. No new ObjectId leaks introduced.

Minor: in refresh_token() at pin_auth.py:357-363, the 'reuse of revoked token' branch logs 'revoking family' but doesn't actually revoke the family — only re-denies the same jti (which is already denied). Comment acknowledges this is by design for now. Future: add user_id field to revoked_tokens and family-revoke on reuse signal.
All raw fetch() calls audited: 7 hits, 100% in allow-list (api.ts, image.ts, chunkedUpload.ts, PinScreen.tsx). No leakage.
